The cost of a newly opened government health center in Pasig City has drawn comparisons to delayed and more costly public works, showing that taxpayers value how their funds are spent.

The Pasig City government inaugurated the E. Santos Health Center on February 27, a three-storey complex complete with CCTV monitoring, fire safety systems, and patient facilities. The structure replaced an older facility within the same complex, which city officials said was “not ideal” and did not have sufficient space or facilities.

The project cost ₱13.5 million and was constructed from March to November 2025, which netizens praised for its cost efficiency. Many drew comparisons to other government projects that cost more and took longer to complete, yet ended up dysfunctional.

For instance, some cited the city-sponsored ₱300-million waiting sheds along Commonwealth Avenue in Quezon City, which have yet to be completed and reportedly fail to protect commuters from rain and heat due to their design. Others recalled a nearly ₱10-million one-storey multipurpose hall with solar panels in Bacoor, Cavite measuring only 80 square meters, which took more than a year to complete.

The widespread comparisons highlight the role of social media in shaping accountability in governance: when taxpayers compare notes on how their local governments handle projects and deliver services, the pressure is on for elected officials to deliver.

Report by Kiara Gorrospe

#radarPHBusiness #radarPH

data.cleaned_text: Sentro sa pulong ng Metro Manila Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (MMDRRMC) ngayong araw ang mga ginagawang hakbang ng pamahalaan ukol sa pagtaas ng presyo ng langis sa gitna ng krisis sa Middle East. Sa pangunguna ni MMDA at MMDRRMC concurrent Chairman Atty. Don Artes, tinalakay ang maigting ng pagbabantay ng pamahalaan sa sitwasyon. Sa direktiba ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr., ang lahat ng oil companies at gasoline stations ay mahigpit na inatasang sumunod sa fuel pricing rules at iwasan ang anumang unauthorized na pagtaas ng presyo, ayon sa Department of Energy (DOE). Mahigpit ding binabantayan ng DOE, katuwang ang iba pang ahensiya at law enforcement agencies, ang mga gasolinahan upang siguraduhing hindi ito nagtatago ng suplay (hoarding) o sobra-sobrang nagtataas ng presyo. Ayon kay Chairman Artes, maluwag na daloy ng trapiko ngayon dahil mas kaunti ang bumabyaheng sasakyan sa kalsada at mas dumarami ang bilang ng mga pasahero sa pampublikong transportasyon. Inatasan niya ang konseho na paghandaan ang epekto ng krisis sa transportasyon, produksyon ng pagkain, at iba pang pangangailangan. Samantala, tinalakay din ang mga paghahanda sa nalalapit na kaganapan tulad ng: • ikakasang transport strike ng grupong PISTON sa Huwebes, Marso 19; • paggunita sa Eid'l Fitr sa Biyernes, Marso 20; • paggunita ng Semana Santa mula Marso 29 (Linggo ng Palaspas) hanggang Abril 5 (Linggo ng Pagkabuhay); • aktibidad at deployment sa ASEAN Summit; • preparasyon at pagtugon sa sakuna, at iba pa. Kasama sa pulong sina George F. Keyser, Senior Chairperson, MMDRRMC at Office of Civil Defense-NCR regional director; Atty. Crisanto Saruca, MMDA Public Safety Office (MPSO) Head, MMDA Planning Office Director Shiela Quingco, at mga miyembro ng MMDRRMC. #mmda #mmdaatyourservice
